requirements.requirement: Configure the opsadmin account on node1 with the supplied SSH public key.
requirements.summary: opsadmin was created, and the supplied ED25519 key was installed in authorized_keys with appropriate ownership and permissions. After the final restart, the account, key fingerprint, and file permissions persisted.

The final effective global and opsadmin-specific sshd policies enable public-key authentication, disable password and keyboard-interactive authentication, and require AuthenticationMethods publickey. A live post-restart negotiation offered only publickey authentication.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. node1 has opsadmin with the specified key, and sshd enforces public-key-only authentication. The final state persisted across a directly observed restart, and the mandatory restart evidence protocol is complete.
limitations: No successful login using the matching private key was captured; the conclusion that the supplied key grants access rests on the observed authorized_keys fingerprint, valid account/file state, effective sshd policy, and live publickey-only negotiation.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory account or sshd configuration files, so those final-state conclusions rely on executor command observations.
The password-status output was redacted in a way that hides the actual status code, although password authentication is independently shown disabled by effective sshd policy and live negotiation.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene was good: package health remained sound, no failed services or unexpected listening sockets appeared, and temporary SSH probe files were removed. The final restart protocol was complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state and acknowledgement, a changed boot ID, recovered sshd/account/key/policy state, and an independently matching final boot identity. One unnecessary broad mutation occurred: an earlier restart was scheduled before the configuration was subsequently replaced with the final global policy; it therefore did not constitute the required post-completion restart and did not contribute to validating the final configuration. Its effects were cleared by later restarts, with no final failed-service or temporary-file residue observed.
